name: @rebosheets/mcp

tools.name: open_workbook
tools.description: Opens an Excel workbook (.xlsx) or a CSV file to read and change it. It is kept in memory: nothing is written until save_workbook. Gives its overview.

path.description: The path of the .xlsx or .csv file.

tools.name: new_workbook
tools.description: Starts an empty workbook with one sheet, to fill and save. Gives it the path it will be saved to.

path.description: Where it will be saved: a path ending in .xlsx or .csv.

sheet.description: The name of its first sheet. "Sheet1" when left out.

tools.name: save_workbook
tools.description: Writes a workbook to a file: Excel (.xlsx) or CSV (.csv, the active sheet as it shows), by the ending of the path. It does not write over a file that is there unless "overwrite" is true: saving a copy under a new name is the safe way.

workbook.description: The path of a workbook opened with open_workbook, or "room:<id>" for one joined. Left out, the last one opened.

path.description: Where to write. Left out, the file it was opened from.

overwrite.description: Write over a file that is already there. False when left out.

tools.name: join_room
tools.description: Works on a workbook people have open in the Rebosheets spreadsheet, through the collaboration server: every change of the tools is seen by them at once, and theirs by the tools. The person shares the address of the server and the id of the room.

url.description: Where the collaboration server is, as "http://127.0.0.1:7440".

name.description: What the people in it see the assistant as. "Claude" when left out.

ticket.description: What the system the workbook belongs to gave, when it asks for one.

tools.name: undo
tools.description: Undoes the last changes the tools made to a workbook that is open, one at a time or several, up to 30.

workbook.description: The path of a workbook opened with open_workbook, or "room:<id>" for one joined. Left out, the last one opened.

tools.name: list_workbooks
tools.description: The workbooks that are open, with whether each has changes not saved.

tools.name: close_workbook
tools.description: Forgets a workbook that is open, with any changes that were not saved.

tools.name: get_overview
tools.description: What the workbook has: its sheets, the block of cells each one uses, how many formulas, merged cells and frozen rows, the first row of each (often its headers) and the defined names. Start here before reading or changing a workbook you have not seen.

workbook.description: The path of a workbook opened with open_workbook, or "room:<id>" for one joined. Left out, the last one opened.

tools.name: read_range
tools.description: Reads a block of cells as a table: rows by their numbers, columns by their letters, each cell as it shows (with its number format) or as its raw value. With formulas true, a cell with a formula shows it after its value. Up to 2500 cells at once: read a big sheet in parts.

workbook.description: The path of a workbook opened with open_workbook, or "room:<id>" for one joined. Left out, the last one opened.

sheet.description: The name of the sheet. Left out, the active one (get_overview says which).

range.description: The block to read. Left out, every cell the sheet uses, by its name as in Excel: "A1:D20", "B5", "C:C" (a whole column) or "3:3" (a whole row).

values.description: "shown" (when left out): as the cells show, "$1,200.00", "28/10/2026". "raw": the values themselves, 1200, 46323.

formulas.description: Show the formula of each cell that has one, as "value ⟨=SUM(A1:A3)⟩". False when left out.

tools.name: read_formats
tools.description: The look of the cells of a block that have one of their own (bold, colours, fill, alignment, number format, borders, merged blocks), and the conditional formats, validation rules and comments the file has on it. To match the look of what is there before adding to it.

workbook.description: The path of a workbook opened with open_workbook, or "room:<id>" for one joined. Left out, the last one opened.

sheet.description: The name of the sheet. Left out, the active one (get_overview says which).

range.description: The block, by its name as in Excel: "A1:D20", "B5", "C:C" (a whole column) or "3:3" (a whole row).

tools.name: find
tools.description: The cells whose value, or formula, has a text in it, in one sheet or in all.

workbook.description: The path of a workbook opened with open_workbook, or "room:<id>" for one joined. Left out, the last one opened.

sheet.description: The name of a sheet to look in. Left out, every sheet.

match_case.description: Tell capitals from small letters. False when left out.

in_formulas.description: Look in the formulas of the cells too. False when left out.

tools.name: evaluate
tools.description: Works out a formula on the workbook without writing it anywhere: to know a total, a count, or whether a lookup finds what it should, before putting it in a cell. Excel's functions, by their English names.

workbook.description: The path of a workbook opened with open_workbook, or "room:<id>" for one joined. Left out, the last one opened.

sheet.description: The sheet its references without a sheet are to. Left out, the active one.

tools.name: write_cells
tools.description: Writes a block of cells from a cell on, row by row, each as a person types it: "=SUM(B2:B9)" a formula (English function names, commas between arguments), "1200" or "1,200.50" a number, "15%" a percentage, "$1,200" money, "2026-10-28" a date, "TRUE" a truth value, anything else a text ("'0123" keeps it a text). An empty string leaves that cell as it is; null clears it. The formats of the cells are kept. Says the values the formulas written give.

workbook.description: The path of a workbook opened with open_workbook, or "room:<id>" for one joined. Left out, the last one opened.

sheet.description: The name of the sheet. Left out, the active one (get_overview says which).

start.description: The cell the block starts at, top left: "A1".

rows.description: The rows, each a list of what goes in its cells from left to right.

tools.name: set_cells
tools.description: Writes cells that are not next to each other, each by its name: {"B10": "=SUM(B2:B9)", "D3": "Paid"}. Each is written as a person types it, as in write_cells. Says the values the formulas written give.

workbook.description: The path of a workbook opened with open_workbook, or "room:<id>" for one joined. Left out, the last one opened.

sheet.description: The name of the sheet. Left out, the active one (get_overview says which).

cells.description: The cells, by their names, and what to write in each.

tools.name: clear_range
tools.description: Clears a block of cells: what is written in them, their formats, or both.

workbook.description: The path of a workbook opened with open_workbook, or "room:<id>" for one joined. Left out, the last one opened.

sheet.description: The name of the sheet. Left out, the active one (get_overview says which).

range.description: The block to clear, by its name as in Excel: "A1:D20", "B5", "C:C" (a whole column) or "3:3" (a whole row).

what.description: "contents" (when left out): values and formulas, the look kept. "formats": the look only. "all": both.

tools.name: format_range
tools.description: Gives a block of cells a look: bold, italic, colours, fill, size and font, alignment, wrapping, a number format and borders. Only what is given changes; false or "" takes a property away. Colours are "#rrggbb". Number formats are Excel's: "#,##0.00", "\"$\"#,##0.00", "0.0%", "dd/mm/yyyy", "General".

workbook.description: The path of a workbook opened with open_workbook, or "room:<id>" for one joined. Left out, the last one opened.

sheet.description: The name of the sheet. Left out, the active one (get_overview says which).

range.description: The block, by its name as in Excel: "A1:D20", "B5", "C:C" (a whole column) or "3:3" (a whole row).

wrap.description: Wrap the text in the cell over several lines.

number_format.description: An Excel number format. "General" takes it away.

borders.description: Thin borders: round every cell, round the block, under it, over it, or none.

tools.name: insert_rows
tools.description: Puts empty rows in before a row. The formulas of every sheet that pointed to the rows moved down move with them, and a range they fall inside grows.

workbook.description: The path of a workbook opened with open_workbook, or "room:<id>" for one joined. Left out, the last one opened.

sheet.description: The name of the sheet. Left out, the active one (get_overview says which).

before.description: The number of the row they go before, from 1.

tools.name: delete_rows
tools.description: Takes rows out; the ones under them move up. A formula that pointed to a cell taken out gives #REF!.

workbook.description: The path of a workbook opened with open_workbook, or "room:<id>" for one joined. Left out, the last one opened.

sheet.description: The name of the sheet. Left out, the active one (get_overview says which).

tools.name: insert_columns
tools.description: Puts empty columns in before a column; the formulas that pointed past them move with the cells.

workbook.description: The path of a workbook opened with open_workbook, or "room:<id>" for one joined. Left out, the last one opened.

sheet.description: The name of the sheet. Left out, the active one (get_overview says which).

before.description: The letters of the column they go before: "C".

tools.name: delete_columns
tools.description: Takes columns out; the ones to their right move left. A formula that pointed to a cell taken out gives #REF!.

workbook.description: The path of a workbook opened with open_workbook, or "room:<id>" for one joined. Left out, the last one opened.

sheet.description: The name of the sheet. Left out, the active one (get_overview says which).

from.description: The letters of the first column: "C".

tools.name: sort_range
tools.description: Sorts the rows of a block by one column or several. Empty cells go last. A first row of headers stays at the top with has_header.

workbook.description: The path of a workbook opened with open_workbook, or "room:<id>" for one joined. Left out, the last one opened.

sheet.description: The name of the sheet. Left out, the active one (get_overview says which).

range.description: The block whose rows to sort, every column of it, by its name as in Excel: "A1:D20", "B5", "C:C" (a whole column) or "3:3" (a whole row).

by.description: The letters of the columns to sort by, the first first: ["C"] or ["B", "D"].

descending.description: From the largest, or Z to A. False when left out.

has_header.description: The first row is headers and stays where it is. False when left out.

tools.name: fill_range
tools.description: Fills a block from the cells at its start, as dragging the corner of a selection in Excel: formulas are copied with their references moved (B2*C2 becomes B3*C3 on the next row), numbers that go up by a step go on by it, a text ending in a number counts on. The way to put one formula down a whole column.

sheet.description: The name of the sheet. Left out, the active one (get_overview says which).

target.description: The whole block to fill, the source in it: "D2:D200", by its name as in Excel: "A1:D20", "B5", "C:C" (a whole column) or "3:3" (a whole row).

sheet.description: The name of the sheet. Left out, the active one (get_overview says which).

range.description: The block, by its name as in Excel: "A1:D20", "B5", "C:C" (a whole column) or "3:3" (a whole row).

tools.description: Sets the width of columns or the height of rows, in pixels (a column is 64 by default, a row 20); "auto" for a column makes it as wide as what is written in it.

at.description: The cell its top left corner goes on.

workbook.description: The path of a workbook opened with open_workbook, or "room:<id>" for one joined. Left out, the last one opened.

sheet.description: The name of the sheet. Left out, the active one (get_overview says which).

workbook.description: The path of a workbook opened with open_workbook, or "room:<id>" for one joined. Left out, the last one opened.

instructions: Tools to read and edit Excel workbooks (.xlsx) and CSV files. Open a file with open_workbook, look at it with get_overview, read it with read_range. Cells go by their names as in Excel ("B12", "A1:D20") and sheets by theirs. Write cells as a person types them in Excel: "=SUM(B2:B9)" a formula with English function names and commas between arguments, "1200" a number, "15%" a percentage, "2026-10-28" a date. To put one formula down a column, write it in the first cell and use fill_range. Formulas are worked out after every change, and the tools that write say what the new formulas give. Changes stay in memory until save_workbook; prefer saving a copy to writing over the original. To work on a workbook people have open in the spreadsheet, join its room with join_room: every change is seen by them at once.
